decision: Open Dashboard Platform Roadmap v1 as the live dashboard umbrella instead of reopening the completed Visual Operating Console v0 roadmap.
rationale: The V0 roadmap closed after the local What Now console shipped. The dashboard now needs a broader V1+ arc covering value-language IA, interactive architecture, review/configuration, optional realtime/team use, and later conversational/multi-agent surfaces. A new tracking parent preserves V0 history while giving current/future work one home.

decision: Sequence V1 as IA shell cleanup first, Architecture view-model work in parallel where isolated, then Architecture shell/page integration.
rationale: The IA and Architecture plans both touch dashboard shell/routing/CSS. Full parallel dispatch would create avoidable merge collisions. Architecture F001 is substrate-only and can proceed while IA cleans branding/nav/copy; Architecture F002+ should integrate after the shell is clean.

decision: Keep V1 dashboard read-only and command-emitter only.
rationale: The dashboard's trust boundary is a product feature. Inline executor, streaming actions, and browser-initiated mutation require a future ADR and belong to V3, not the V1 product-surface cleanup and Architecture Explorer work.

decision: Make value-first language a platform invariant, not a one-page copy pass.
rationale: Non-technical reviewers, founders, and product owners must understand what is blocked, what needs approval, and whether the system is safe before encountering internal DontPanic nouns. Technical IDs and commands stay available in secondary detail for agents and operators.

decision: Treat Firebase/realtime dashboard work as optional V4 adapter work.
rationale: The local dashboard must remain useful without Firebase setup. Firebase is appropriate when team/shared visibility or remote governed mutation is justified, not as a prerequisite for the default operator console.

decision: Do not draft V2-V5 child plans until their trigger conditions fire.
rationale: Review/Evidence, Decisions Queue, Configuration, Local Executor, Agent Session Registry, realtime collaboration, multi-agent compare, and conversational authoring are plausible but not equally ready. Trigger-gated children preserve the small-lockable-plan discipline that worked for capability operations and planning intelligence.

decision: Dashboard child plans use docs/design/<plan-id>/ as non-runtime design asset intake.
rationale: Claude Design and similar tools may produce mockups, tokens, JSX, screenshots, copy decks, and interaction notes. These artifacts are accepted as design inputs under docs/design/<plan-id>/; implementation ports tokens and small components to the existing dashboard runtime, while full-page mockups remain visual specifications rather than runtime dependencies.

decision: Ingest Claude Design v3 as a roadmap-level design pack with per-child manifests.
rationale: The v3 package spans both V1 child plans: shell/value-language/fleet/core pages for IA and Architecture Explorer pages/variants for the architecture plan. Store the package once under docs/design/dashboard-platform-roadmap-v1/claude-design-v3/ and use per-child manifests to declare ownership without duplicating binary assets.
